findings.reason: decodeSecretKey decodes again whenever isBase64 passes (a multiple of 4 long, only [A-Za-z0-9+/=]). utils/kubernetes.py:1428-1429 generates 16-character passwords from letters, digits and !@#$%^&*, so any all-alphanumeric password (about 14% of them) decodes cleanly into wrong bytes, and authentication then fails.
findings.claim: decodeSecretKey base64-decodes the already-decoded secret value again whenever it looks like base64, corrupting valid passwords.
findings.evidence: client-go already returns decoded Secret.Data. The code then runs `if isBase64(decoded) { base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(decoded) … return string(b) }`. isBase64 accepts any string whose length is a multiple of 4 and that uses only [A-Za-z0-9+/=]. The operator generates passwords as 16 characters from letters+digits+"!@#$%^&*" (utils/kubernetes.py:1428-1429), so (62/70)^16 ≈ 14% of them are 16 alphanumeric characters. Those pass isBase64, decode successfully to 12 random bytes, and get sent as the password. A user-chosen existingSecret password such as "Password1234" is mangled the same way. The operator's own reconciler decodes only once (keycloak_reconciler.py:1315-1320).

members.claim: Cluster credential resolution corrupts valid credentials that happen to look like base64, causing authentication to fail.
members.evidence: ResolveFromCluster passes the already-decoded Secret.Data values through decodeSecretKey, which decodes them again whenever isBase64 succeeds. A legitimate password such as "YWJjZGVm" becomes "abcdef" before authenticate sends it to Keycloak; there is no explicit indication that the secret was double-encoded.

findings.reason: importer.go parses added/skipped/errors and never reads 'overwritten', so OVERWRITE runs would report zero. Whether Keycloak's response ever contains 'errors' or ERROR actions depends on the external API, and nothing in the repo (no recorded response or test) settles it.
findings.claim: The errors>0 check and the ERROR/FAILED result actions may not exist in Keycloak's Partial Import response, and overwritten counts are never parsed.
findings.evidence: importResp parses `errors` and collects results whose Action is "ERROR" or "FAILED" (line 217). Keycloak's PartialImportResults reports added/skipped/overwritten, with result actions ADDED/SKIPPED/OVERWRITTEN; failures come back as non-200 HTTP. `overwritten` isn't parsed at all, so an OVERWRITE run prints Added 0 / Skipped 0. No test exercises importBatch against a real or recorded response.

findings.reason: ImportUsers returns nil on importBatch error and on token-refresh error (importer.go:76-83). printImportSummary in cmd/import_users.go returns immediately when result is nil, which defeats the 'Print partial result' comment.
findings.claim: An HTTP-level batch failure or token-refresh failure returns a nil result, so the progress from earlier batches, which are already committed, is never shown.
findings.evidence: `batchResult, err := importBatch(...); if err != nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("batch %d/%d failed: %w", ...) }`. In cmd/import_users.go:162 the comment says "Print partial result before returning error so user can see progress", but printImportSummary returns immediately when result == nil. The partial result is printed only on the `errors > 0` path, which may never fire (see the previous finding).
